game.title: Day One: CS Student Snapshot
game.description: A first-day ice-breaker to explore your interests, background, and goals as a CS student. Most questions have no wrong answer — just be honest!

questions.prompt: Which area of computer science excites you most right now?
How would you honestly describe your coding experience heading into this course?

options: Just starting out — this is pretty new to me
I know the basics of one or two languages
I've built a few real projects on my own
I'd consider myself an experienced developer

questions.prompt: What kind of project would excite you most to build during your time here?

options: A polished mobile or web app
A data analysis or ML tool
Something low-level: an OS, compiler, or language

questions.prompt: I have written code outside of class — just for fun or a personal project, not because it was assigned.
What's your biggest concern as you start this CS program?

options: The math and theory will be too hard
I'll feel behind compared to my peers
Balancing coursework with everything else in life
Figuring out what kind of CS career I actually want

questions.prompt: How do you learn new technical skills best?

options: Just building something and figuring it out

questions.prompt: What programming language do you feel most comfortable in right now? (Type 'none yet' if you're just starting out.)
Where do you picture yourself five years after graduation?

options: At a large tech company (big enterprise / FAANG-style)
At a startup — maybe one I co-founded
I honestly have no idea yet

questions.prompt: Binary search on a sorted list of one million items requires at most about 20 comparisons. True or false?
Which of these data structures gives O(1) average-case lookup time?
Which of the following are core principles of object-oriented programming (OOP)? Select all that apply.
Which of these tools or technologies have you already used before starting this program? Select all that apply.

options: A web framework (React, Django, Flask, etc.)
